verdicts.reason: A has a clear left-to-right banner: product, then a dominant 30% OFF, then the CTA. But the SUNSET SALE eyebrow and Q logo are shrunk into a tiny footer row, and the ellipse and circle are cropped at the bottom edge. B blows the fine print up nearly to body-copy size and turns SUNSET SALE into a large label below the headline, so the hierarchy is inverted. B's logo is also jammed under the CTA, and its bottom ellipse is heavily cropped.

Its fine print is almost as big as the subhead, 'delivery.' is orphaned on its own line, and the right half is just a product box, which makes it lopsided. B (the same layout as pair 1 A) keeps a clean hierarchy with the CTA prominent, though the logo, eyebrow and legal line are tiny and the shapes are cropped at the edges.
